properties.name: Evidence carries the date it was taken, so a measurement can be aged rather than believed forever
properties.statement:
Where the design records that something was MEASURED, it must also record WHEN — so a report can say "measured, but a long time ago" instead of presenting a stale number as current.

THE OBSERVATION IS `fact:defect-a-measured-contribution-carries-no-date-so-it-is-believed-forever` (music_graph F22); this is the intent behind fixing it.

THE ASYMMETRY IS THE ARGUMENT, and it is reflow2's own doctrine applied unevenly. `ver:evidence-quality` has a whole TIME axis — an accept dated after the check reports STALE, a re-run after the accept is current, and an undated side is UNKNOWN and counted rather than silently passed. `Artifact.last_confirmed_at` exists for exactly this, and its description says a confirmation "says nothing changed" so it is stored as a dated property. ⇒ Dating evidence is settled practice for Verification and for Artifact, and absent from the one number a KPP verdict rests on: the CONSTRAINS edge declares `note`, `contribution` and `basis` and NO DATE.

MEASURED THEIR SIDE: a contribution recorded as 6.9 fps with `basis: measured` against a 40 fps minimum, while the true measured value was 55.06. The number was right when taken and had been wrong for days. Their framing is the one to keep — "an estimate stays an estimate, but a measurement is a statement about a system at a moment."

⚠️ `basis: measured` IS THE STRONGEST EVIDENCE CLAIM THE SCHEMA OFFERS AND THE ONLY ONE THAT DECAYS. An estimate does not go stale; a measurement does.

NOT DECIDED, and both are real: whether the date belongs on the edge or on a separate observation node — the same question `Artifact.last_confirmed_at` answered by choosing the property, on the grounds that confirmations are high-frequency non-events; and whether ageing against the contributors' artifact checksums is sound, since a contribution can go stale with no file changing.

A SECOND, SMALLER ITEM IN THE SAME REPORT, kept because it cost them real time: a MINIMUM budget returns `within` while a contributor is `unstated`. That is defensible — a missing number can only improve a minimum — but the asymmetry is unexplained in the payload and read as a bug. The verdict is right and does not say why it is right.
